title: My Thoughts Are Not Your Thoughts
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: The incarnation is only astonishing when we grasp how completely other God is. The author of the stars took on a human mind and heart.
exhortation: The miracle of God becoming like us isn't all that miraculous unless we grasp how completely different, how other, God is. When he declares, "My thoughts are not your thoughts," pause and consider the scale of that.

What does an all-knowing, all-powerful being even think about? A single thought of God's would overload our little human brains. His thoughts carry the weight of all human history, all the heavenly realms created before man existed, and all the complexities of angelic beings and their hosts. He knows the thoughts of every person alive right now, everyone who ever lived and everyone yet to be born. To say his ways are not our ways is a massive understatement. He thinks in an infinitely complex way no human could approach.

The best we can do is imperfect analogies: the height of the heavens, the infinity of the stars, the mystery of black holes that blows our minds. But God isn't just a student of these things. He is their author. And science, far from closing the gap between Creator and creature, keeps proving that every layer of the universe we uncover is ten times more complex than we understood. From the spinning of electrons to the spark of a cell, we are just scratching the surface of his craftsmanship.

It is against this backdrop, the infinite scale of his creation, his thoughts and his ways, that we see the beauty of the gospel. The God who authored the stars placed his infinite thought into a human mind. The Creator became the created. He took on a human heart and walked the earth. This morning, let's stand in awe of our indescribable, incomprehensible, infinitely good God.
prayer: Lord, it is astounding to think that you would leave your throne above, the one who created the world, the heavens and the stars, the sea and the earth, and become a weak human to bear our sin, our shame and our punishment. The wrath of the Father that should have been poured out on us was poured out on Jesus.

Fill us with gratitude and zeal for you today, so that we seek to glorify you in our lives and in the world, and spread your fame and your indescribable goodness and grace to a world in need. Open our eyes. In Jesus' name.
